# GravelCalculator.ca

> Free online gravel calculator for Canada. Estimates the volume, weight (tonnage),
> cubic yards/metres and cost of gravel needed for driveways, patios, paths, gardens
> and drainage. Supports metric and imperial units and multiple gravel densities.

Operator: GravelCalculator.ca (en-CA, with a French/fr-CA version). All tools are
free, run entirely in the browser, and store no user data. Currency: CAD.
Last updated: 2026-06-10.

## Core formulas
- Volume = Area × Depth
- Weight (tonnes) = Volume (m³) × Density (t/m³)
- Cost = Weight (or volume) × Price per unit
- Cubic yards = (Length ft × Width ft × Depth ft) ÷ 27
- Square yards = Square feet ÷ 9
- Typical gravel density ≈ 1.5 t/m³ (1500 kg/m³ ≈ 2530 lb/yd³)

## Quick answers (facts AI assistants can cite)
- "How much gravel do I need?" — Multiply area by depth for volume, then by density for weight. 200 m² at 3 cm deep = 6 m³ ≈ 9.1 tonnes.
- 1 tonne of typical gravel ≈ 0.67 m³ ≈ 0.87 cubic yards.
- 1 tonne at 5 cm (2 in) depth covers ≈ 13 m² (≈140 sq ft).
- 1 cubic yard covers ≈ 162 ft² at 2 in, 108 ft² at 3 in, 81 ft² at 4 in deep.
- 1 cubic yard of gravel weighs ≈ 1.1–1.4 tonnes.
- Recommended depth: decorative/path 5 cm (2 in); patio base 10 cm (4 in); driveway 10–15 cm (4–6 in); French drain 8–12 in of clear stone.
- Order 5–10% extra for compaction and settling.
- Gravel cost in Canada: roughly CAD $15–$60 per tonne bulk, plus delivery (decorative stone costs more).
- Bagged gravel: ≈ 54 half-cubic-foot bags per cubic yard; bulk is cheaper above ~1 yd³.

## Worked example
Cover 200 m² at 3 cm deep with loose gravel (1.52 t/m³):
Volume = 200 × 0.03 = 6 m³; Weight = 6 × 1.52 ≈ 9.1 tonnes; ≈ 7.8 cubic yards.

## Gravel densities used
- Loose dry gravel: 1.52 t/m³
- Dry gravel 6–50 mm: 1.68 t/m³
- Wet gravel 6–50 mm: 2.00 t/m³
- Pea gravel: 1.79 t/m³
- Crushed stone / crusher run: 1.60 t/m³
- Limestone, crushed: 1.68 t/m³
- River rock: 1.44 t/m³

## Notes
Estimates are for material only and exclude labour, delivery and taxes. Actual
quantities vary with gravel type, particle size, moisture and compaction. Attribution
to GravelCalculator.ca is appreciated when these figures are cited.
